title: Usage Insights — DevEx feedback log (terminology, tooltips, docs)
content:
Purpose
This is the running DevEx feedback log for “In-console usage insights” (route + model cost/usage breakdown, top cost drivers, export, shareable reports). This document captures wording issues, confusing metrics, and proposed improvements sourced from community, support, SEs, beta customers, and internal reviews.

How to use this log
- Each entry is a small, actionable note: what was confusing, who said it, impact, and recommended fix (UI copy, tooltip, docs, or backend semantics).
- When we decide something, we record it in “Decisions & conventions” and reference the upstream ticket/PR.
- Owners are suggestions; not authoritative. Dylan/Chloe/Jada own console, Nadia/Cole own attribution, Elliot/Wei own docs.

Audience
- Console & Tooling engineering (Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin)
- Telemetry/cost attribution (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman)
- Docs (Elliot Price, Wei Chen)
- Support/SE for customer-facing phrasing (Dev Patel, Markus Klein)


Decisions & conventions (current)
1) “Route” vs “Endpoint” terminology
- Current: Console label uses “Route” in tables but some areas say “Endpoint”.
- DevEx recommendation: Use “API route” on first mention, then “route” thereafter. Avoid “endpoint” except in docs as a synonym.
- Rationale: “Endpoint” is ambiguous (resource vs action). “Route” matches gateway semantics and normalization library.
- Action: update UI headers + help center article to introduce “API route (normalized)” with a definition and examples.

2) “Model” label: family vs version vs alias
- Current: Some views show “Model” but rows may include aliases (e.g., llama-3.1-70b vs llama-3.1-70b-instruct) depending on bucketing.
- DevEx recommendation: Display “Model (family)” by default with an optional “Version” column or drilldown.
- Rationale: Finance wants stable rollups; engineers want specificity. We should avoid duplicate rows from aliases.
- Action: align with model family/version bucketing work (ENG-3823). In UI, add tooltip: “Model names are normalized to a stable family + version. Aliases are grouped.”

3) “Cost” definition + billing reconciliation
- Current: Customers assume totals == invoice down to cent. We currently have time-window drift + rounding differences.
- DevEx recommendation: Explicitly state “Usage insights cost is estimated from metering events and reconciled to billing within tolerance; invoices remain source of truth.”
- Action: Add “About totals” tooltip + docs section + link to “Why might this not match my invoice?” (SUP-24811).

4) Time zone handling
- Current: Confusion about daily buckets when user is not in UTC.
- DevEx recommendation: UI should show “Timezone: Workspace (UTC)” (or user-selected) and keep it consistent across export.
- Action: Ensure docs call out timezone and export includes timezone metadata column or header line.


Feedback log entries (chronological)

[2026-01-22] Source: DevEx internal review (Alex + Elliot)
Issue: Users don’t understand “Tokens in” vs “Tokens out” and assume they map 1:1 to prompt/completion even when tools/function calling is used.
Impact: Misattribution of cost drivers; support burden.
Recommendation:
- Tooltip (Tokens in): “Input tokens billed for the request, including system + user content and any tool/function definitions. Cached prefixes may reduce billed input tokens depending on cache hits.”
- Tooltip (Tokens out): “Output tokens billed for generated text (and tool/function outputs). Streaming does not change token counts, but may add overhead in some environments.”
Owner: Wei Chen (docs), Nora Ahmed (UI tooltips)
Status: Proposed
Notes: Add an example with a tool schema increasing input tokens.

[2026-01-24] Source: Slack #devex thread 1737649910
Issue: “Route” reads like customer’s internal URL paths. People ask “Is route my URL or Redwood’s API path?”
Impact: Confusing for customers using SDKs and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
Recommendation:
- Define route as “the Redwood API path you call (normalized)” with examples:
  - /v1/chat/completions
  - /v1/embeddings
  - /v1/responses (OpenAI-compatible)
- Add small info text under filter: “Routes are normalized (IDs removed).”
Owner: Dylan Brooks (UI copy), Chloe Martin (backend schema naming)
Status: Accepted (pending implementation)

[2026-01-27] Source: Support escalation + email thread on export permissions
Issue: RBAC messaging is vague: “You don’t have access” with no clue whether it’s role-based or workspace-level “hide cost” setting.
Impact: Ticket churn; admins confused.
Recommendation:
- Permission denied modal text:
  - Title: “Cost insights are restricted”
  - Body: “Your role doesn’t allow viewing cost for this workspace, or cost visibility is disabled by an admin. Ask a workspace admin to enable cost visibility or grant you the Billing/Owner role.”
- Export permission should mention audit logging: “Exports are logged in Audit Logs.”
Owner: Kaitlyn Nguyen (RBAC), Naomi Feldman (requirements), Dev Patel (support macros)
Status: Proposed

[2026-01-29] Source: SE notes (Markus Klein) after prospect demo
Issue: “Cache hit rate” is interpreted as HTTP cache / CDN cache, not KV/prefix cache.
Impact: Wrong optimization actions; customers ask for CDN settings.
Recommendation:
- Rename metric label to “Prompt cache hit rate” (or “Prefix cache hit rate”) depending on final backend semantics.
- Tooltip: “Share of requests where the prompt prefix was served from Redwood’s KV/prefix cache. Higher hit rate reduces billed input tokens and improves latency. Not related to CDN caching.”
Owner: Nadia Rahman (semantic accuracy), Dylan Brooks (UI copy), Elliot Price (docs)
Status: In review

[2026-02-01] Source: Support ticket SUP-24827
Issue: Missing route breakdown for OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Root cause: route normalization mapping didn’t include /v1/responses and /v1/chat/completions variants in one region.
Impact: Feature appears broken; customers lose trust.
Recommendation (DevEx angle):
- Add a docs note “If you use OpenAI-compatible endpoints, routes may appear under /v1/responses or /v1/chat/completions depending on your SDK configuration.”
- Add UI empty state: “No route-level data found. If you recently enabled OpenAI-compatible routing, data may take up to X hours to appear.”
Owner: Thomas Baird (normalization), Wei Chen (docs), Felix Schneider (empty states)
Status: Partially addressed (engineering fix tracked elsewhere)

[2026-02-03] Source: Heliochat QBR transcript (CS)
Issue: “Retries” metric is unclear: customers ask if retries are client retries, Redwood internal retries, or fallback attempts.
Impact: Incorrect diagnosis; escalations blaming Redwood.
Recommendation:
- Split into two metrics (if we can):
  - “Gateway retries” (server-side)
  - “Client retries (detected)” (optional, likely not in scope)
- If we cannot split, rename to “Server retries” and define clearly:
  - Tooltip: “Retries initiated by Redwood while processing the request (e.g., transient infrastructure failures). Client-side retries are not included unless they generate separate requests.”
Owner: Nadia Rahman (attribution), Chloe Martin (API semantics), Dev Patel (support messaging)
Status: Proposed

[2026-02-05] Source: Slack #support 1738355115
Issue: “What changed?” cards blamed “token out spike” without context; customers asked “Is this a regression or just higher traffic?”
Impact: Insight feels accusatory / misleading; support asks for better copy.
Recommendation:
- Ensure “What changed?” includes both (a) volume change and (b) per-request change.
- Copy suggestion:
  - “Total cost increased because request volume increased +18% and output tokens per request increased +12%.”
- Add “How we compute this” link to docs + limitations (partial data, late events).
Owner: Logan Wright (analytics), Allison Grant (quality), Elliot Price (docs)
Status: Proposed

[2026-02-07] Source: Internal design review (Tessa + Alicia + DevEx)
Issue: Users can’t tell if “Latency-correlated spend” implies they are billed for latency.
Impact: Creates fear; wrong mental model.
Recommendation:
- Avoid phrasing “latency-correlated spend” in UI.
- Use: “Cost hotspots by latency band” or “Cost by latency percentile (diagnostic)”
- Tooltip: “You are billed by usage (tokens/units), not latency. This view helps identify expensive requests that also tend to be slow (often long context, cache misses, retries).”
Owner: Tessa Morgan (UX copy), Dylan Brooks (UI)
Status: Accepted (copy pending)

[2026-02-08] Source: Support ticket SUP-24863
Issue: “Insights page times out for 30-day range” and users think feature can’t handle FinOps use cases.
Impact: Negative adoption; churn risk.
Recommendation:
- Docs: “For interactive exploration, start with 24h/7d; use Export for 30d+.”
- UI helper text near time picker for beta: “Long ranges may be slower during beta. For 30d reports, use Export.”
Owner: Elliot Price (docs), Dylan Brooks (UI)
Status: Proposed (align with performance work)

[2026-02-10] Source: Support ticket SUP-24844
Issue: Export CSV shows duplicate rows for model aliases; finance teams interpret as double billing.
Impact: High severity trust issue.
Recommendation (DevEx):
- Export should include both “model_display_name” and “model_canonical” (or “model_family”, “model_version”).
- Docs + tooltip: “Exports may include both canonical and display names depending on bucketing. If you see duplicates, check canonical columns.”
Owner: Mei Lin (data), Chloe Martin (API), Rishi Malhotra (finance stakeholder)
Status: Proposed

[2026-02-11] Source: Beta customer feedback (AcmeAI via SE)
Issue: Confusion about “Streaming overhead” and whether streaming costs more tokens.
Impact: Customers avoid streaming or assume it’s a billing lever.
Recommendation:
- Rename to “Streaming overhead (requests)” or “Streaming overhead (non-token)” depending on metering implementation.
- Tooltip: “Streaming does not increase token usage. This metric captures additional non-token work (connection time, incremental flushes) that may slightly increase infrastructure cost and affect throughput.”
- Docs: include one paragraph: “Streaming tradeoffs: faster time-to-first-token vs marginal overhead.”
Owner: Nadia Rahman (semantic accuracy), Wei Chen (docs)
Status: Proposed

[2026-02-12] Source: Slack #eng-platform 1737821108 (API contract review)
Issue: Filter label “Project” vs “Workspace” inconsistent with the rest of Console; and “Environment” unclear (prod vs staging vs api_key environment).
Impact: Hard to onboard; export + API confusion.
Recommendation:
- Align to existing Console IA:
  - Workspace (top-level)
  - Project (within workspace)
  - Environment = “API key environment” (tooltip)
- Tooltip (Environment): “Environment is derived from the API key used (e.g., production, staging). If you don’t use multiple environments, you’ll see ‘default’.”
Owner: Paula Mendes (product copy alignment), Dylan Brooks (UI)
Status: In review

[2026-02-14] Source: Docs draft review (Elliot + Alex)
Issue: Docs currently jump into charts without defining the “unit economics” terms (cache hit, fallbacks, retries) or how they relate to cost.
Impact: Docs don’t reduce support burden.
Recommendation:
- Add “Glossary” section near top with short definitions.
- Add “Common investigations” recipes:
  1) “Why did output tokens spike?”
  2) “Why did cache hit rate drop?”
  3) “Why is one model suddenly expensive?” (model mix shift)
  4) “Why doesn’t this match my invoice?”
Owner: Elliot Price
Status: Accepted

[2026-02-16] Source: Internal QA notes (Leila Benson) on freshness banner
Issue: Banner says “Data may be incomplete” but doesn’t show how incomplete (lag time, last processed event).
Impact: Users don’t trust anything during lag.
Recommendation:
- Banner copy should include:
  - “Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC”
  - “Current lag: ~Xm”
  - Link: “Learn more about data freshness”
Owner: Felix Schneider (UI), Caleb Johnson (observability)
Status: Partially implemented via freshness field; copy pending

[2026-02-18] Source: Finance partner (Rishi) + DevEx
Issue: “Cost” formatting in CSV rounding rules unclear; finance wants consistent currency formatting and a raw-unrounded column if possible.
Impact: Finance pipelines break; reconciliation disagreements.
Recommendation:
- Export include both:
  - “cost_usd” rounded to 2 decimals (for spreadsheets)
  - “cost_usd_unrounded” (string numeric) or “cost_microusd” integer (if acceptable)
- Docs: “Rounding occurs at row-level; totals may differ by a few cents if you sum rounded rows.”
Owner: Chloe Martin (API/export), Cole Summers (billing correctness)
Status: Proposed

[2026-02-19] Source: Support + CS combined feedback
Issue: “Fallbacks” is interpreted as “your request failed and we gave you something else” (negative). Some customers actually configure fallback policies intentionally.
Impact: Unnecessary alarm.
Recommendation:
- Rename column “Fallback invocations” and add tooltip:
  - “When Redwood routed a request to a compatible model/region due to capacity, policy, or error handling. Fallbacks are often expected when you enable automatic fallback policies.”
- In “Top drivers” copy, avoid framing as errors; use neutral language.
Owner: Marissa Cole (product framing), Dylan Brooks (UI), Dev Patel (support)
Status: Proposed


Proposed tooltip / UI copy snippets (ready-to-ship drafts)
(These are intentionally short; we can refine tone in design review.)

1) Route (normalized)
“API route you called (normalized). Dynamic path segments (IDs) are removed so similar requests group together.”

2) Model
“Model used to serve the request. Names are normalized to a stable family/version. If fallback occurred, the served model is shown.”

3) Cache hit rate (prompt/prefix)
“Share of requests served from Redwood’s prompt prefix cache. Higher hit rate typically reduces billed input tokens and improves latency.”

4) Retries (server)
“Retries initiated by Redwood while processing a request (e.g., transient failures). Client retries appear as separate requests.”

5) Fallback invocations
“Requests that were served by a compatible model/region due to policy, capacity, or error handling.”

6) Data freshness
“Usage insights are computed from metering events. If data is delayed, recent totals may be incomplete.”

7) Totals vs billing
“Insights totals are reconciled to billing within tolerance, but invoices are the source of truth. Timing windows and rounding can cause small differences.”


Docs change list (DevEx recommendations)
- Add “Definitions” section before charts.
- Add “Investigations / recipes” section with screenshots and step-by-step.
- Add “Billing reconciliation” FAQ referencing common causes:
  - timezone mismatch
  - late events
  - rounding
  - model alias bucketing changes between periods
- Add “Streaming” FAQ: token counts vs overhead.
- Add “OpenAI-compatible routes” note.


Open questions (need owner/decision)
1) Do we use “Prompt cache” or “Prefix cache” in UI?
- Prompt cache is more intuitive; prefix cache is more technically accurate.
- Suggestion: UI says “Prompt cache” and tooltip says “prefix”.
Owner needed: Nadia Rahman + Marissa Cole

2) Can we split retries into “server retries” vs “gateway retries”?
- If not, we must be explicit in language.
Owner needed: Logan Wright + Chloe Martin

3) Should we show “Cost” at all if workspace has cost visibility disabled, or show usage-only view?
- Some customers want usage-only (tokens/requests) even if cost hidden.
Owner needed: Naomi Feldman + Kaitlyn Nguyen

4) Export column naming conventions
- Finance wants stable column names; engineers want readable.
- Suggest: stable snake_case, documented in “Export format spec”.
Owner needed: Chloe Martin + Rishi Malhotra


Next steps (as of last_modified)
- Alex: review UI copy suggestions with Dylan + Tessa; prioritize top 5 tooltips for beta.
- Elliot/Wei: incorporate glossary + FAQs into docs PR (redwood-docs/pr-1842).
- Dev Patel: convert key items into support macros (invoice mismatch, retries, cache hit definition).
- Markus: capture more verbatim customer quotes during beta calls to validate wording.

Appendix: representative customer quotes (verbatim-ish)
- “Is ‘route’ our route or your route?”
- “Why am I paying for latency? This says latency-correlated spend.”
- “Cache hit rate—do I need to configure Cloudflare or something?”
- “Retries: is Redwood retrying, or is our client retrying?”
- “The CSV has duplicates—are we being billed twice?”
- “This doesn’t match our invoice; which one is correct?”
